text:
Aisha Bello: For the mixed-workload scheduler canary, we need additional alerting around long-queue starvation + queue depth. Right now we only page on overall request latency + generic saturation and that’s not enough if the long queue starts backing up silently.

Aisha Bello: Can we align on paging thresholds today so we can wire this into the canary checklist?

Rafael Mendes: +1. During overload tests last week we saw long queue depth climb while p95 for short looked “fine” until it wasn’t. We need a page signal earlier.

Tomáš Novák: What metrics do we have available (or soon) from runtime? I saw PR for histograms but not sure what’s landed in perf-canary yet.

Julian Moore: From PR_8444 (in review) we’ll have:
- `runtime.scheduler.queue_depth{class="short|long"}` (gauge)
- `runtime.scheduler.queue_wait_ms_bucket{class=...}` (hist)
- `runtime.scheduler.dequeue_total{class=...}` (counter)
- `runtime.scheduler.starvation_events_total` (counter) + `runtime.scheduler.max_wait_ms{class=...}` (gauge, sampled)

Julian Moore: Naming is still not 100% final but that’s the shape.

Omar El-Sayed: Also we can derive backlog slope: `rate(queue_depth)` + compare to `dequeue_total`. For canary, simpler might be queue depth + max wait.

Sean Gallagher: We should page on “we are actively starving” vs “we are getting close.” Queue depth can be noisy under burst.

Peter Holtz: +1. Queue depth alone pages too much. If we have `max_wait_ms{class="long"}` that’s a more direct starvation signal.

Aisha Bello: Proposed paging signals:
1) Long-queue starvation: `max_wait_ms{class="long"} > 8000` for 3m (page)
2) Long-queue backlog: `queue_depth{class="long"} > 300` for 10m (page)
3) Long-queue backlog warning: same depth threshold but 5m (slack-only)

Aisha Bello: Question is whether 8s/300 are sane.

Sofia Ivanova: For the scheduler policy we’ve been using a fairness window target of ~2s under typical load, but in overload we can go higher. 8s feels like a definite “something is wrong” threshold.

Sofia Ivanova: Depth threshold depends on batch + arrival rate. On A100 runs we saw long depth hovering 50–120 during stress; 300 is probably “bad.”

Rafael Mendes: I’m ok with `max_wait > 8s` paging. For depth, could we also require it to be increasing? Like depth > 300 AND `rate(depth[5m]) > 0`.

Felix Schneider: We can do that in PromQL. Example:
`runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class="long"} > 300 and deriv(runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class="long"}[10m]) > 0`

Felix Schneider: (deriv might be too sensitive; could use `predict_linear` too.)

Logan Wright: Heads up: `max_wait_ms` gauge is sampled (not exact max over all queued reqs) unless you compute it from the hist. If you want more reliable alerting, use the histogram quantile of wait.

Omar El-Sayed: Good point. We can page on `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(queue_wait_ms_bucket{class="long"}[5m])) by (le)) > 8000`.

Tomás Novák: That’s probably safer. “Max” gauges are always a trap :)

Aisha Bello: Ok, revised proposal:
- PAGE: `p99(queue_wait_ms){class="long"} > 8000ms` for 5m
- PAGE: `queue_depth{class="long"} > 300` for 10m AND increasing (some slope condition)
- WARN (no page): `queue_depth{class="long"} > 200` for 10m

Aisha Bello: And we should add a non-paging alert for short queue too, but don’t want to overdo it.

Sean Gallagher: I like it. Also, we need a “no service” condition: if long dequeue rate drops to ~0 while depth is non-zero, that’s pathological.

Peter Holtz: +1. That’s exactly the starvation failure mode.

Felix Schneider: We can add:
`rate(runtime_scheduler_dequeue_total{class="long"}[5m]) < 0.1 and runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class="long"} > 50` for 5m (page)

Sofia Ivanova: That’s a great canary guardrail. If long dequeue is near-zero while queue exists, the fairness window isn’t being enforced or a bug like priority inversion.

Rafael Mendes: Can we scope paging to canary only initially? I don’t want a new global pager storm if metrics aren’t stable.

Aisha Bello: Yes—these will be enabled only on the canary job / canary cluster dashboards while flag is on. Once we’re confident in noise levels we can discuss broader enablement.

PagerDuty: [auto] Acknowledged action item: Add mixed-workload scheduler starvation/backlog alert rules (canary-only) (owner: Aisha Bello)

Tomás Novák: Can someone drop the exact metric names once they merge? I’ll update the rollout runbook with “if page fires do X” steps.

Julian Moore: I’ll post final names once PR lands. Likely prefix will be `redwood_runtime_scheduler_...` in Prometheus (we map `runtime.scheduler.*` -> snake_case). I’ll sync with Felix.

Omar El-Sayed: Also note: we should split alerts by route/tier if possible. Some Dedicated canaries have very different mixes. But for prototype canary, cluster-level is fine.

Sean Gallagher: Decision: ship canary-only paging for long queue wait p99 > 8s (5m), long dequeue rate ~0 while depth>50 (5m), and backlog depth>300 for 10m with positive slope; plus warning at depth>200.

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: I’ll implement these in the alert pack + link in ENG-4829. Felix/Julian please @ me on final metric names when ready.
